stem: Which physical finding is most consistent with Cushing syndrome rather than primary adrenal insufficiency?

options.A: Diffuse hyperpigmentation with weight loss, salt craving, and persistent hypotension.
options.B: A rounded face with upper-body weight gain and increased fat at the base of the neck or between the shoulders.
options.C: Enlarged hands and jaw with coarse facial features and increased shoe size.
options.D: Cold intolerance, bradycardia, constipation, and generalized weight gain.

rationale: NIDDK describes common physical changes of Cushing syndrome as weight gain, a round face, increased fat around the base of the neck, and a fatty hump between the shoulders, often with thin limbs, purple striae, bruising, and muscle weakness. In contrast, primary adrenal insufficiency/Addison disease commonly causes weight loss, low blood pressure, salt craving, and skin darkening. Therefore B is the finding most consistent with Cushing syndrome rather than primary adrenal insufficiency. C is more consistent with acromegaly and D with hypothyroidism.
educational_objective: Differentiate cortisol excess from primary adrenal insufficiency by recognizing the characteristic Cushing pattern of central/upper-body weight gain, rounded face, and cervicodorsal fat accumulation.
source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), NIH
source_document_title: Cushing's Syndrome; Symptoms & Causes of Adrenal Insufficiency & Addison's Disease
source_version_date: Current NIDDK endocrine information live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Cushing's Syndrome > Symptoms: weight gain, round face, increased fat around base of neck, fatty hump between shoulders, wide purple stretch marks and muscle weakness. Adrenal Insufficiency/Addison's Disease > Symptoms: weight loss, low blood pressure, salt craving; Addison's disease may cause skin darkening.
source_claim_supported: Rounded face with upper-body/neck/upper-back fat accumulation is characteristic of Cushing syndrome, whereas weight loss, hypotension, salt craving and hyperpigmentation favor primary adrenal insufficiency.

source_original.stem: Which physical finding is most consistent with Cushing syndrome rather than primary adrenal insufficiency?

options.A: Diffuse hyperpigmentation with weight loss, salt craving, and persistent hypotension.
options.B: A rounded face with upper-body weight gain and increased fat over the upper back.
options.C: Enlarged hands and jaw with coarse facial features and increased shoe size.
options.D: Cold intolerance, bradycardia, constipation, and generalized weight gain.

source_original.rationale: Cushing syndrome commonly causes upper-body weight gain, a rounded face, and increased fat over the upper back and above the collarbones. Weight loss, hyperpigmentation, hypotension, and salt craving are more characteristic of primary adrenal insufficiency.
source_original.source_detail: Symptoms and physical changes: upper-body weight gain, rounded face, and fat accumulation around neck/upper back. Live NIDDK page currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, emergency response and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the endocrine-differentiation construct and key B, tightened the Cushing fat-distribution wording to the current NIDDK description and explicitly contrasted Addison findings, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests recognizable endocrine phenotype patterns.

distractor_audit.A: Favors primary adrenal insufficiency/Addison disease rather than Cushing syndrome.
distractor_audit.C: Favors acromegaly rather than cortisol excess/deficiency.
distractor_audit.D: Favors hypothyroidism rather than Cushing syndrome.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B contains the characteristic Cushing fat-distribution/rounded-face pattern specifically contrasted with primary adrenal insufficiency.
